analyticalMisses.summary: BAL ML + BAL 6+ repeated essentially the same Baltimore/Coors narrative from 8/31 -- both lost both days. A clear example of series/narrative anchoring rather than fresh independent evidence.

SD ML: the cross-book market picture was conflicted before the bet -- that should trigger INVESTIGATE/REDUCE/PASS, not a full-size wager pushed through the disagreement. This bet also could not be canonically imported (no displayed probability/price was ever recorded for it) -- see Import gap. LOSS, -$30, preserved here narratively but not linked to a canonical betId.

The 9/1 5-leg parlay lost only because SD ML lost. Combined with 8/31's 5-leg combo also going 4/5, this is NOT evidence that 5-leg parlays are good -- future parlays should generally use only the 3-4 strongest independent legs, not a marginal 5th leg for payout.

analyticalWins.summary: CWS was the cleanest analytical win of the two-day sample: Sean Burke threw 5.2 scoreless (1 H, 4 BB, 6 K); the independent pregame read liked his underlying profile relative to the opposing starter and liked the CWS offense. Both the F5 and ML expression of that thesis won.
CLE F5 was a clean starter-driven thesis: Gavin Williams delivered an excellent outing (13 K).
PHI F5 was a clean starter/matchup win.
NYY ML: a starter/team edge translated cleanly into a full-game win.

gameLevelConcentration.note: BAL ML + BAL 6+ runs repeated essentially the same Baltimore/Coors narrative as 8/31 -- both legs lost both days. SERIES/NARRATIVE ANCHORING, not independent evidence.
CWS F5 + CWS ML both won on the same clean Sean Burke starter thesis -- MODERATELY_CORRELATED (same underlying game/starter edge expressed twice), the day's cleanest analytical win.

performanceByMarketFamily.note: CLE, PHI and CWS F5 all won -- clean starter/matchup-driven wins. User's exact-cost-basis figure was +$71.11 (cost basis $74.99, using CLE F5's $39.99 share-card cost); canonical whole-dollar-stake basis gives +$71.10 on $75 risk, a $0.01 artifact of the same cost-vs-canonical-stake rule as 8/31's ML family.

PIT/CWS/NYY ML won, BAL ML lost. User's originally-reported ML family also included SD ML (LOSS, -$30 stake) for a 3-2 record and +$17.23 P/L; SD ML could not be canonically imported (see Import gap) so this family here reflects only the 4 linked ML bets. 47.23 + (-30.00, SD ML's stake/net) = 17.23, exactly reconciling to the user's original figure -- the entire gap is that one bet.
BAL 6+ runs lost, repeating the same Baltimore/Coors scoring narrative as 8/31's BAL 6+ loss -- series/narrative anchoring across consecutive days on the same underlying team.

5-leg ML combo (SD/PIT/CLE/TEX/CWS) went 4/5, losing only on the SD ML leg -- the same leg that also failed to canonically import as a standalone bet (see Import gap). Combined with 8/31's 5-leg combo also going 4/5, this is NOT evidence that 5-leg parlays are good; future parlays should generally use only the 3-4 strongest independent legs.

processErrors.summary: PIT ML WON the ticket (13-12) but the mechanism was not clean. RESULT=WIN, PROCESS=MIXED -- a winning ticket is not by itself proof the handicap mechanism worked.

manual-20260901-sdcin-sd-ml-003 (SD ML, stake $30, LOSS, paid $0) could not be written through the canonical importer: no displayed probability, cents price, or maxPayout was ever reported for it, and entryPrice/entryOdds is a required field this system refuses to invent. Process lesson: every manual wager needs its displayed price/probability captured at bet time, not reconstructed after the fact -- especially for a bet the postmortem itself flags as having a conflicted pregame market picture.

proposedInvestigations.summary: Review whether capping fun parlays at 3-4 strongest independent legs (vs. 5) measurably changes long-run parlay ROI once more data accumulates -- 2 data points (8/31, 9/1) is not sufficient to conclude anything about leg count yet.
